messages.content: Calculate the resistance of a wire with a length of 5m and cross sectional area 0.01m² with resistivity of copper and aluminum

function.name: calculate_resistance
function.description: Calculate the resistance of a wire using resistivity, length, and cross-sectional area. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

length.description: The length of the wire in meters.

area.description: The cross-sectional area of the wire in square meters. This is a float type value.

resistivity.description: Resistivity of the material (Default: 'copper'). Allowed values: 'copper', 'aluminum'

We need to call the function once per calculation. Provide two calls or combine into one? The function signature expects single object; we can pass different parameters each time. So produce two separate outputs maybe as JSON array? But instructions say "When you do not know how to answer ...". We have knowledge. We'll compute manually too but better to rely on tool. Let's call it twice:

First call: length=5, area=0.01, resistivity='copper'.
Second call: same but resistivity='aluminum'.

We'll output results accordingly. Use the tool invocation format exactly. Then after receiving responses, present them nicely.
